Last Friday (the 21st), when the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case was delivered, police escorted a woman who was queuing for a seat in the public gallery into a police vehicle during the early hours. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intention."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of having a shirt with somewhat seditious intent," and took her away in a police vehicle. While officers were removing the woman, several police officers kept directing reporters to leave, telling them "we'll take you to the press area," and pulled the orange cordon line towards the direction of Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, the cordon was taken down. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

集誌社 (Chikit Journal) enquired with the police as to why the woman was taken away and whether an arrest had been made. In response this morning (the 24th), the police stated that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Court on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intention," and was detained for investigation.
